quizzes.title: Rules 2026 and Sports Bodies
quizzes.passage: The National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026 are meant to enhance transparency, inclusivity and accountability in sports administration in India. The Rules apply to national sports bodies, which include the national committees that oversee Olympic and Paralympic sports as well as the federations that govern particular sports at the national level. Under the Rules, every national sports body must have a General Body and an Executive Committee. The General Body must include sportspersons of outstanding merit, and a specified share of those sportspersons must be women. The Executive Committee must also include women members. The Rules set conditions that govern who may hold office in these bodies, and they limit how long a person can serve, using both a number of years and an upper age limit. Members therefore serve for a fixed period and must continue to meet the conditions laid down in the Rules. Taken together, the provisions are intended to make the governance of national sports bodies more transparent and accountable. The framework also includes a National Sports Board, which is described as the apex regulatory body for sports governance in India. The framework itself forms part of the National Sports Governance Act, whose key institutional mechanisms came into force from January 2026.

questions.q: Which body is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India?
questions.explanation: The National Olympic Committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India.

questions.q: What share of the sportspersons of outstanding merit in the General Body must be women?
questions.explanation: Under the Rules, 50% of the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit in the General Body must be women.

questions.q: Which authority notified the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026?
questions.explanation: The Union Government notified the Rules, 2026.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Information about recognised national sports bodies can be sought under the RTI Act 2005.
Reason (R): Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005, which is why information about them can be sought under it.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. National Paralympic Committee   ->   A. 3 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
II. Term of members   ->   B. Sole governing body for Paralympic sports
III. Executive Committee   ->   C. Minimum age of 25 years
IV. Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit   ->   D. At least 4 women members
questions.explanation: The National Paralympic Committee is the sole body for Paralympic sports, and the term, Executive Committee women and minimum age facts match II-A, III-D and IV-C.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about national sports bodies under the Rules:
I. Regional sports federations are among the other bodies governed under the Rules.
II. A person who has been convicted by a court and sentenced to imprisonment is disqualified from holding office.
III. The National Olympic Committee is the sole governing body for Paralympic sports.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II reflect the Rules, while III wrongly gives Paralympic sports to the National Olympic Committee instead of the National Paralympic Committee.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Members serve for 3 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
II. The National Paralympic Committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India.
III. Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit in the General Body must be at least 25 years of age.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II wrongly assigns Olympic sports to the National Paralympic Committee.

quizzes.title: Rules 2026 Recall
quizzes.passage: Sports administration in India is organised through national sports bodies, and the framework that governs them was strengthened recently. The stated objectives are transparency, inclusivity and accountability. Each national sports body is expected to have two organs, a General Body with a wide membership and an Executive Committee. The General Body is to include sportspersons of outstanding merit, a group defined partly by age and partly by achievement. A specified proportion of this group must be women. The Executive Committee must also have women members, and the minimum is fixed by the framework. Members hold office for a fixed term, which ends either after a set number of years or on reaching an upper age limit, whichever comes first. Bodies recognised under the framework are treated as public authorities for the purposes of information law. Separate federations govern particular sports at the national and regional levels, while the committees for the Olympic and Paralympic movements have their own responsibilities. The framework also includes a board that regulates the recognition of sports bodies. The framework applies to national sports bodies across the country, whatever the sport they govern. Together these provisions describe both the structure of national sports bodies and the qualifications of the people who serve in them.

questions.q: What is the minimum age, in years, of a Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit in the General Body?
questions.explanation: Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit must be at least 25 years of age under the Rules.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of women members that the Executive Committee must include?
questions.explanation: The Rules require the Executive Committee to include at least 4 women members.

questions.q: Members serve for 3 years or up to what age, whichever is earlier? (age in years)
questions.explanation: The term of members is 3 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: Which committee is the sole governing body for Paralympic sports in India? (name)
questions.explanation: The National Paralympic Committee is the sole governing body for Paralympic sports.

questions.q: Under which Act are recognised sports bodies deemed public authorities? (Act and year)
questions.explanation: Recognised sports bodies are deemed public authorities under the RTI Act 2005.

questions.q: Which committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India? (name)
questions.explanation: The National Olympic Committee is the sole governing body for Olympic sports in India.

questions.q: What percentage of the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit in the General Body must be women? (number, without the % sign)
questions.explanation: At least 50% of the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit in the General Body must be women.

quizzes.title: National Sports Tribunal
quizzes.passage: The National Sports Tribunal was set up to resolve disputes in sport. Its stated purpose is to provide a forum that is independent and speedy. The Tribunal's functioning is linked to the wider framework of the National Sports Governance Act, which introduced several institutional mechanisms for sports administration in India. The Tribunal does not hear every type of dispute, because its jurisdiction is defined by the framework and certain categories of matters are kept outside it. Some matters that relate to sport are handled under separate laws and procedures, and the Tribunal's role must be understood in that context. The Tribunal has a defined structure, with a head and other members who bring relevant knowledge to its work. Its purpose, scope and structure together show how the framework seeks to bring clarity and order to the settlement of sports disputes in the country. The key institutional mechanisms of the Act came into force from January 2026. The Rules and mechanisms under the Act aim to enhance transparency, inclusivity and accountability in sports administration. The Tribunal is therefore one of several bodies created to strengthen sports administration in India. Its work is part of that framework and is expected to be read alongside the Rules that apply to national sports bodies.

questions.q: Along with being independent and speedy, which two adjectives describe the Tribunal's intended resolution of sports disputes?
questions.explanation: The Tribunal is meant to provide independent, speedy, effective and cost-efficient resolution of sports disputes.

questions.q: Under which Act do doping-related disputes fall exclusively?
questions.explanation: Doping-related disputes fall exclusively under the National Anti-Doping Act 2022, outside the Tribunal.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT among the fields from which the Tribunal's two other members are drawn?
questions.explanation: The two other members are experts in sports, public administration or law.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The National Sports Tribunal can hear disputes arising during the Olympic Games.
Reason (R): Disputes arising during major international sporting events such as the Olympic Games are excluded from the Tribunal's jurisdiction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Disputes during major international events like the Olympic Games are excluded, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Election disputes   ->   A. Excluded from the Tribunal's jurisdiction
II. Doping-related disputes   ->   B. Within the Tribunal's jurisdiction
III. Disputes during the Asian Games   ->   C. Sitting or retired Supreme Court judge or Chief Justice of a High Court
IV. Head of the Tribunal   ->   D. Governed by the National Anti-Doping Act 2022
questions.explanation: Election disputes are within the Tribunal's jurisdiction, doping disputes fall under the National Anti-Doping Act 2022, Asian Games disputes are excluded, and the head is a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge or High Court Chief Justice.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Sports Tribunal:
I. Governance matters fall within the jurisdiction of the Tribunal.
II. Disputes arising during the Commonwealth Games are within the Tribunal's jurisdiction.
III. Athlete selection issues fall within the Tribunal's jurisdiction.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Governance matters and athlete selection issues are within the jurisdiction, but Commonwealth Games disputes are excluded.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Disputes arising during the Olympic Games are excluded from the Tribunal's jurisdiction.
II. Doping-related disputes are heard by the Tribunal under the National Anti-Doping Act 2022.
III. Election disputes are within the Tribunal's jurisdiction.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because doping disputes fall outside the Tribunal under that Act.

quizzes.title: Tribunal Recall
quizzes.passage: The National Sports Tribunal forms part of a larger set of changes to how disputes in sport are handled in India. Its stated purpose is to deliver decisions that are independent and speedy. The Tribunal is set up under the framework of the National Sports Governance Act, whose key institutional mechanisms came into force from January 2026. Its jurisdiction is limited, and several kinds of matter are kept outside it. Some matters relating to sport are dealt with under separate laws, so the Tribunal does not handle every dispute that arises in the sporting world. The Tribunal has a head and a number of other members, and each member is expected to bring relevant knowledge to the work. The Tribunal's structure, purpose and scope show how the framework seeks to bring clarity to sports dispute resolution. A wide range of matters can reach it, but only those that fall within its defined areas. The framework as a whole is intended to improve how sports bodies are run, and the Tribunal is one of its key parts. The Tribunal's work is therefore closely connected with the other mechanisms introduced under the Act, which together form a single framework for sports governance in India.

questions.q: Apart from a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge, which other office can head the Tribunal? (post)
questions.answer: Chief Justice of a High Court
accept: Chief Justice of a High court
questions.explanation: The Tribunal may be headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge or a Chief Justice of a High Court.

questions.q: Under which Act do doping-related disputes fall? (name of the Act with year)
questions.explanation: Doping-related disputes fall exclusively under the National Anti-Doping Act 2022.

questions.q: Which major multi-sport event held in Asia is excluded from the Tribunal's jurisdiction? (name)
questions.explanation: Disputes arising during the Asian Games are excluded from the Tribunal's jurisdiction.

questions.q: The Tribunal's stated aim pairs 'independent' and 'speedy' with 'effective' and one more word. What is that word? (one word)
questions.explanation: The Tribunal is meant to provide independent, speedy, effective and cost-efficient resolution of sports disputes.

questions.q: Which kind of dispute, relating to who is picked to represent a team, falls within the Tribunal's jurisdiction? (two words)
questions.explanation: Athlete selection issues fall within the Tribunal's jurisdiction.

questions.q: Which kind of dispute, relating to the conduct of votes in sports federations, falls within the Tribunal's jurisdiction? (one word)
questions.explanation: Election disputes are within the Tribunal's jurisdiction.

questions.q: Apart from the head, which court's sitting or retired judge can head the Tribunal? (court name)
questions.explanation: A sitting or retired judge of the Supreme Court can head the Tribunal.

quizzes.title: Sports Initiatives and Performance
quizzes.passage: India's sports sector is coordinated through the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, which serves as the nodal ministry for sport. The National Sports Policy sets out three broad aims: to improve the quality of sports training, to promote participation in sport, and to increase the number of athletes competing internationally. A range of government initiatives works towards these aims, and they operate at different levels of sport. Some are directed at the wider population, while others focus on particular groups, such as young people. Indian athletes have recently won medals in major international competitions, including the Paris Olympics and the Paris Paralympics. India has also produced strong results in chess, and players from the country have reached the top of international competition. The initiatives in this area are therefore not limited to a single sport or a single age group. Each one has its own purpose, and together they form part of the framework through which the government seeks to strengthen Indian sport in the country. The government's approach therefore combines broad participation programmes with more targeted support for athletes who have reached the highest level. Each of these measures has a specific target group, and the groups differ in age and level of performance.

questions.q: Which scheme identifies and supports athletes with potential to win medals at the Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: TOPS identifies and supports athletes with potential to win Olympic medals.

questions.q: Which initiative encourages mass participation in fitness activities?
questions.explanation: The Fit India Movement encourages mass participation in fitness activities.

questions.q: Which Indian athlete won bronze in two 10 metre air pistol events at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
questions.explanation: Manu Bhaker won bronze in the Women's and Mixed 10 metre air pistol events at Paris.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Viswanathan Anand was the first Indian Grandmaster to win the FIDE World Chess Championship.
Reason (R): D Gukesh was the first Indian to win the FIDE World Chess Championship.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Gukesh was the second Indian Grandmaster to win the title, after Viswanathan Anand, so R is false while A is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Khelo India   ->   C. Defeated China's Ding Liren in the 2024 FIDE World Chess Championship
II. Mission Olympic Cell   ->   A. Gold in high jump at the 2024 Paris Paralympics
III. Praveen Kumar   ->   D. Works within the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports
IV. D Gukesh   ->   B. Identifies and develops athletes at grassroots and elite levels
questions.explanation: Khelo India works at grassroots and elite levels, the Mission Olympic Cell is within the ministry, Praveen Kumar won Paralympic high jump gold, and Gukesh beat Ding Liren.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian sports initiatives:
I. KIRTI is aimed at school children aged 9 to 18.
II. India won two silver medals at the Paris Olympics.
III. Khelo India was launched in 2017.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: KIRTI targets children aged 9 to 18 and Khelo India began in 2017, while India won only one silver medal at Paris.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. TOPS was launched in 2014.
II. KIRTI is meant for athletes above the age of 18.
III. D Gukesh became world champion at the age of 18.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because KIRTI targets school children aged 9 to 18.

quizzes.title: Initiatives Recall
quizzes.passage: Sport in India is supported by government programmes that cover different stages of an athlete's development. The National Sports Policy aims to improve the quality of training, to encourage wider participation in sport, and to increase the number of athletes who compete at the international level. Some initiatives reach the general public and encourage people to take part in fitness activities. Others concentrate on finding talent early, by searching among students across the country. A separate set of schemes focuses on athletes who already have the ability to compete for medals at the top level. Financial support for training, coaching and international competition is an important element of this support. A dedicated cell also monitors and supports the preparation of athletes for the Olympics. India's results in recent major events show the scale of this effort. Indian athletes have won medals at the Paris Olympics and the Paris Paralympics, and an Indian player has become world champion in chess at a very young age. The programmes described here operate at different levels, from broad participation to elite performance, and each has a distinct role in the wider system. Each of these measures has a specific target group, and the groups differ in age and level of performance.

questions.q: Which initiative launched in 2024 identifies talent among school children aged 9 to 18? (acronym)
questions.explanation: KIRTI, launched in 2024, targets school children aged 9 to 18 to identify talent.

questions.q: In which year was the TOPS scheme launched? (year)
questions.explanation: The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) was launched in 2014.

questions.q: How many silver medals did India win at the Paris Olympics? (number)
questions.explanation: India won 1 silver and 5 bronze medals at the Paris Olympics.

questions.q: Who won gold in high jump at the 2024 Paris Paralympics? (name)
questions.explanation: Praveen Kumar won gold in high jump at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.

questions.q: Which player did D Gukesh defeat in the 2024 FIDE World Chess Championship? (name)
questions.explanation: D Gukesh defeated China's Ding Liren in the 2024 FIDE World Chess Championship held in Singapore.

questions.q: The Mission Olympic Cell operates within which ministry? (name)
accept: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
questions.explanation: The Mission Olympic Cell is within the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports and supports athletes under TOPS.

questions.q: Which initiative launched in 2017 identifies and develops athletes at grassroots and elite levels? (name)
questions.explanation: Khelo India, launched in 2017, identifies and develops athletes at grassroots and elite levels.
